usage.callShape: POST https://graphadvocate.com/route with JSON body {"request": "<plain-English blockchain data question>"}

inputExample.request: What is the latest price of USDC on Uniswap v3 on Base?

usage.outputShape: body.recommendation (recommended service), body.reason, body.query_ready.args (ready-to-run GraphQL + subgraph_id), body.execution_result.data.data (LIVE executed query results — e.g. token, bundle.ethPriceUSD, tokenHourDatas[].priceUSD), body.alternatives[], body.get_started (free API key URL). The actual answer to your question is usually pre-executed inside body.execution_result.data.data.
quirks: The request field MUST be named 'request' (not 'query', 'text', or 'prompt'). Wrong field name still returns HTTP 200 but with {error:'Missing request text', hint:'POST {request: your query} or A2A format'} — and YOU STILL PAY for that failed call. Always send {"request": "..."}.
x402 paid even on the bad-field-name response (200 + error body), so the field name is money-critical.

The response is a recommendation engine: it picks the best subgraph/API for your plain-English question AND pre-executes the GraphQL for you. Read body.execution_result.data.data for the live answer; body.query_ready/curl_example are for if you want to re-run it yourself.
Response includes a body.promoted_skills array advertising other paid GraphAdvocate endpoints (polymarket/hyperliquid scoring) — ignore unless relevant.
qa-pay reported confirmed:false / txHash:null (settlement not captured on-chain in this harness), but status 200 and live data confirm the call succeeded.
usage.guide: POST to https://graphadvocate.com/route with JSON body {"request": "<your plain-English blockchain data question>"} — payment is x402 USDC ($0.01) on Base, no API key needed. CRITICAL: the field must be named "request"; using "query" or any other name returns a 200 hint-error AND still charges you. Read the live answer from body.execution_result.data.data, which contains the pre-executed GraphQL result; body.recommendation/query_ready/curl_example tell you which subgraph it used and how to re-run it yourself with a free thegraph.com API key.
